newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Filipino lawmaker charged with rape of 11-year-old.
newsitem.headline: Filipino lawmaker charged with rape of 11-year-old.

text.p: Philippine prosecutors on Tuesday filed charges of statutory rape against a congressman from President Fidel Ramos's ruling coalition, accusing him of sexual relations with an 11-year-old schoolgirl.
Justice Secretary Teofisto Guingona said the state would ask for the death penalty for Romeo Jalosjos, a member of the House of Representatives.
Jalosjos, in a petition filed in court by his lawyers, called the charges a "fairy tale" and accused prosecutors of bowing to media pressure "to satisfy one's appetite for blood".
Manila newspapers broke news of the case in August at a time of public uproar over crimes involving politicians and other prominent people thought to be beyond the reach of the law.
Jalosjos was charged with two counts of statutory rape and 12 counts of lascivious acts against the girl.

Prosecutors said in documents filed with the Makati Regional Trial Court that the acts were committed in Jalosjos's Manila apartment. They said he paid the girl amounts ranging up to 10,000 pesos ($385) each time she visited him and promised to make her a movie star.
The girl's father brought her to the politician in exchange for money, they said. The father faces a separate charge of child exploitation.
A brother of Jalosjos, who closely resembles the lawmaker, had told police he was the one who had had dealings with the girl, using his brother's name.
Prosecutors said the girl's evidence incriminated the congressman.

The charges will be heard later this month by a judge who will decide whether to send the case for trial and whether to issue a warrant of arrest against the congressman, Justice Department officials said.
